subject: Dedicated vs Hyperscaler evaluation \u0014 POC scope & next steps
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@openretail.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated vs Hyperscaler evaluation - POC scope & next steps

Hi Daniel -

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment:

Key requirements you shared:
- Predictable sustained throughput for real-time scoring (95th pct latency targets)
- Reserved capacity/commit for peak retail hours with predictable cost
- VPC integration + customer-managed keys
- Ability to fail over to another region or burst pool without degrading SLAs

Where Redwood helps vs hyperscaler managed endpoints:
- Dedicated Reserved Pools: we can reserve a GPU pool (example: 4x A100 equiv) for you with SLA-backed throughput guarantees instead of ephemeral spot/auto-scaling only.
- Tail-latency controls: our routing + caching and per-token batch tuning keeps 95th/99th percentile latency predictable for LLM workloads.
- Cost predictability: committed monthly capacity + clear overage pricing (we'll share a template). Hyperscalers often have less predictable autoscale-driven costs for very spiky traffic.
- Private deploy + VPC: we support private control planes and customer KMS for regulated data.

Proposed POC (2 weeks):
1) Reserved pool: provision a dedicated pool equivalent to 4xA100 for the POC window.
2) Tests: sustained throughput tests (qps), tail-latency under production-like prompts, failover/regional fallback, and cost-per-1k-tokens comparison vs their current hyperscaler baseline.
3) Deliverables: test runbook, latency/throughput dashboard, cost comparison, and SOW for production rollout.

Action items / next steps:
- Confirm scope (GPU count & target SLAs) - can you confirm 4 GPUs looks right for the initial POC?
- I'll loop in our infra and pricing owners and share a draft SOW + capacity comparison.
- Tentative kickoff: Tue Oct 27 (we can shift if you need more lead time).

I'm attaching a short capacity comparison and a first-draft SOW for review.

Thanks - talk soon.

Markus Klein
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0118

Attachments: capacity-compare.xlsx, SOW-draft-v1.pdf

From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@openretail.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated vs Hyperscaler evaluation - POC scope & next steps

Markus -

Great recap, thanks. A couple of clarifying questions before we lock scope:

1) Pricing model: is the POC billed as a trial credit or billed at a prorated committed rate? For production, what does the commit + overage structure look like (monthly invoice, annual commit)?
2) VPC integration: we need to ensure the model servers sit inside our VPC with no egress for customer PII. Is that supported for Dedicated?
3) Sustained throughput: our baseline is ~120 qps sustained with spikes to 500 qps during peak. If we reserve 4 GPUs, will that meet the sustained numbers or do we need a different sizing approach?
4) Can you share a sample SLA and any references for customers using Reserved pools?

I attached our requirements export (requirements.csv).

If we can get answers to pricing and VPC/KMS today, I'll confirm availability for the Oct 27 kickoff.

Thanks,
Daniel Park
Head of ML, OpenRetail
daniel.park@openretail.com

Attachment: requirements.csv

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@openretail.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-19T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated vs Hyperscaler evaluation - POC scope & next steps

Daniel - thanks for the fast follow-up. Answers inline: 

1) POC billing: we can run the POC under a temporary credit arrangement (no charge) if you prefer a short eval, or we can bill it as a prorated committed month. For production we typically do a monthly or annual commit (you pick the term) with an overage rate per GPU-hour if utilization exceeds the commit. I can have finance send two sample pricing options (monthly commit vs annual) by EOD.

2) VPC & KMS: yes - Dedicated supports private control plane and model-serving instances in your VPC with customer-managed KMS/HSM. No egress for PII is a supported configuration; we will include a network diagram in the SOW.

3) Sizing for throughput: 120 qps sustained with spikes to 500 qps - 4xA100-equivalent is likely tight for sustained 120 qps depending on model size and prompt length. Our infra team recommends sizing around 6 GPUs for comfortable headroom for that workload; we can run a quick benchmark during POC to validate. If you'd like, we'll size the reserved pool to 6 for the POC and show cost delta vs 4 so you can decide.

4) SLA & refs: attaching a sample SLA and a SOC2 summary. We also have a customer (retail vertical) reference we can introduce; let me know if you'd like an intro.

Proposed tweak to POC: provision a 6-GPU reserved pool for two weeks, run the throughput + tail-latency tests, and produce a cost comparison vs your current hyperscaler baseline. If that sounds good I will:
- Finalize the SOW with Laura (scope & network diagram)
- Schedule kickoff for Oct 27
- Share pricing options and the SOW/PO terms

Looping Laura and Dylan to confirm SOW adjustments and booking.

Best,
Markus

Attachments: SLA-sample.pdf, SOC2-summary.pdf

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Markus / Dylan -

Thanks - I can take the SOW and update scope to 6 GPUs for the POC and add the VPC network diagram + KMS section. A few items I need from you to finish the SOW:
- Confirm target SLA numbers (95th pct token latency target, and desired uptime % for the POC window) - Markus, can you propose the language?
- Payment terms for the POC (credit vs prorated invoice) - I'll put both options in and flag the preferred.
- Legal: I'll include standard data processing addendum and the SOC2 reference link.

I'll have a draft SOW back by EOD Monday Oct 20. Markus - once I share the SOW, could you confirm Daniel's procurement contact for the PO?
